6 questions. Click an answer to check it: you will see right away whether it is correct, with a short explanation. Nothing is saved.

::: {.sb-quiz-q data-answer="1"}
**1.** A model predicts the price of a house from its surface and its number of rooms. What kind of problem is it?

::: {.sb-quiz-options}
- A classification problem
- A regression problem
- A clustering problem
- A dimensionality reduction problem
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-explain}
The target (a price) is a continuous number: it is a **regression**. Classification predicts a category, clustering and dimensionality reduction are unsupervised (there is no target).
:::
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-q data-answer="1"}
**2.** Why do we split the data into a training set and a test set?

::: {.sb-quiz-options}
- To train the model faster
- To measure how the model performs on data it has never seen
- Because scikit-learn requires it
- To remove the outliers
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-explain}
The test set plays the role of new data. A score computed on the training data is too optimistic: the model has already seen these examples.
:::
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-q data-answer="2"}
**3.** Which preprocessing steps must be **fitted** on the training set only?

::: {.sb-quiz-options}
- None: they don't learn anything
- Only the model
- The imputer, the scaler and the encoder, like the model
- Only the encoder
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-explain}
An imputer learns means or medians, a scaler learns means and standard deviations, an encoder learns categories. Fitting them on the test set would leak information from the test set: use `fit_transform` on the training set and `transform` on the test set.
:::
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-q data-answer="2"}
**4.** A column `Country` contains `France`, `Spain` and `Germany`. What does a `OneHotEncoder(drop='first')` produce?

::: {.sb-quiz-options}
- One column with the values 0, 1 and 2
- Three columns of 0s and 1s
- Two columns of 0s and 1s
- Nothing: text columns must be removed
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-explain}
One-hot encoding creates one 0/1 column per category. With `drop='first'`, the first category is dropped: it is implied when all the other columns are 0, and it avoids perfectly correlated columns.
:::
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-q data-answer="1"}
**5.** Why should the target **never** be imputed?

::: {.sb-quiz-options}
- Because scikit-learn can't do it
- Because the model would learn from values we invented
- Because it would make the dataset too small
- It can be imputed, like any other column
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-explain}
An imputed target is a made-up answer: the model would learn it and the evaluation would measure it. Rows with a missing target are dropped.
:::
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-q data-answer="1"}
**6.** After `preprocessor.fit_transform(X_train)`, why does `X_train.head()` fail?

::: {.sb-quiz-options}
- Because the preprocessing failed
- Because the result is a NumPy array, not a pandas DataFrame
- Because `head` needs a number
- Because the data is now empty
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-explain}
`ColumnTransformer` returns a NumPy array: pandas methods are not available anymore. Use `X_train[0:5]`, or get the column names with `get_feature_names_out()`.
:::
:::

::: {.sb-quiz-score}
